#4846. 23 Christmas Decoration Ideas, From Traditional Tartans to a Jewel-Toned Winter Wonderland

“Seeing holiday decor get a modern-design makeover is my Roman Empire,” says home expert Julian Thomas. These Christmas decoration ideas will set a festive tone in any room of the house—and yes, it’s possible to deck your halls in an elevated way. “In the past, if you decorated for the holidays you had to sacrifice style and aesthetics for nostalgia and Christmas necessities,” he says. “Not any more. From silk tree skirts to Clivia marble stocking holders, Christmas decorations have never been chicer.”

But if you’re more of a traditionalist, you’ll find inspiration to fit your style here, too. In fact, multiple design pros we spoke to mentioned that this year’s big trend is nostalgia (more on that below). With retro inspiration as well as new takes on festive color palettes, plus creative Christmas garlands and interior design-friendly stockings, here are 23 Christmas decor ideas for all kinds of merrymakers.

A dark and moody space shouldn’t stop you from merry decor for the holiday season—lean into it with your Christmas decorations.

“Red and green are traditional Christmas colors, but I love to break away from tradition a bit and use bright jewel tones to create a dramatic and sophisticated look for the holiday season,” says Annie Sloan, paint and color expert and creator of Chalk Paint. She is a fan of purple—once reserved for kings and emperors—for the holidays. “My Tyrian Plum Wall Paint is a rich, jewel-toned plum with maroon and red elements,” she says. “It works beautifully with metallics, fairy lights, and flickering candlelight to create a Christmas fit for the three kings!”

Glass jars of gelt and dreidels set a stylish holiday vignette.

For an easy DIY project, fill glass jars with small holiday decor items, like dreidels or gold coins, as seen in this Hanukkah-adorned living room arranged by LA-based designer Ethan Charles Greenfeld of Ethan Charles Design. Pinecones, tiny Christmas ornaments, bows, or mini Santa figures would all make great options as well.

Centering your tree in the entryway sets a festive tone right away.

Get more bang for your balsam by placing it in a spot in your living room that’s visible from other areas of the house—even better if you can see it from your home’s entryway. “I love making an impact with my tree and recommend putting it front and center if you can,” says designer Lauren Ashley of Lauren Ashley Experiences in Houston. “The tree is only up for a few weeks, so why not showcase it right at your entrance if there’s room?” Not only will guests get a peek at all your trimmings, you can enjoy the tree each time you come and go from your home.

Carry Christmas cheer throughout the house with wreaths and bows.

“I like to decorate the rooms we spend the most time in since Christmas decor just makes me so happy,” says lifestyle blogger and content creator Miyaeva Renae. “This year, I’m planning to decorate our living room, kitchen, bedroom, nursery, and even the bathrooms to bring that festive feeling throughout the house.” Here, Renae has wrapped kitchen cabinets in bows and placed mini wreaths on the backs of island chairs. Other small touches—like a wreath on the range hood, ribbon tied around a utensils jar, and a bowl filled with pinecones—add even more holiday cheer.

For those who leave gifts under the tree for a little while before Christmas day, it’s worth considering how the paper fits in with your decorative scheme.

This will inspire you to get your wrapping done early, and it gives your gift boxes another purpose: dressing up your living room before the big exchange on Christmas morning. “I love to make my own gift wrap,” Sloan says. “Buy cheap brown packing paper and paint it yourself with stripes, spots, or any design you fancy. Add contrasting ribbons and pile your gifts under the tree. Your gifts become part of your Christmas scheme. It’s stunning.” By making your own wrapping paper, you can also make sure it perfectly complements the rest of your decor.

Holiday-themed decals are a good—and renter-friendly—way to get your space looking festive.

For big impact without big effort, consider a high-quality wall sticker like the Victorian-inspired Christmas variety from Wallpick. “No tools are needed to apply Wallpick’s stickers, however I do recommend applying them to smooth walls for the best results,” says Wallpick’s founder Dina Jasmin. Use a wall sticker to frame your Christmas tree. Or, if a tree isn’t in the plans, the sticker can serve as a focal point and place to gather presents.

A Christmas tree, garland, wreath, and throw pillows add some Christmas cheer to this otherwise calm, neutral bedroom.

Wake up in a winter wonderland by hanging a wreath above the bed and wrapping bed posts in a garland and string lights. Throw pillows featuring trees or snowflakes add a further festive touch—and if you really want to go all out, put a pre-lit Christmas tree in your bedroom as well. This year, Renae is even extending the Christmas home decor beyond the primary suite: “I usually don’t decorate our guest bedroom, but since we’ll have family staying with us this, I’m planning to add some holiday touches there too along with all of the bathrooms,” she says. “It’s such a fun way to make every space feel festive and welcoming.”

What’s better than one Christmas tree in your entryway? Two.

“I love to host, so it’s not uncommon for friends and family to gather at my house throughout the season,” says Wendy Lau, Yale Home’s interior design consultant. While living rooms and dining areas may pull focus when it comes to Christmas decoration ideas, Lau greets guests with yuletide flair upon arrival: “One of my favorite places to decorate for the holidays is the entryway.” She uses a smart lock programmed with custom codes to help guests feel right at home, so they can see themselves in and be dazzled by eye-catching visuals like “greenery and twinkle lights—always a charming sight. I also like to drape garlands over the doorway and hang big wreaths with a jolly red bow out front.” A holiday-themed doormat at the front door as part of the porch decor completes the festive first impression.

This felt ball garland is a creative departure from the traditional greenery.

Hang strings of felt balls, dried oranges, yarn tassels, or stars cut from heavy-stock paper as an alternative to traditional pine or cedar garlands. Or, Thomas says, “Mid- to high-tier retailers like CB2 and West Elm use modern shapes and materials to create some very unique and trendy garlands, like one made of crystal shapes and another with gold-frosted palm fronds.”

Metallics are a fun, nontraditional way to set an icy winter scene in your space this holiday scene.

“Metallics can add a sophisticated touch to holiday decor,” says Houston-based interior designer Chandos Dodson Epley of Chandos Collective. “Gold, silver, and bronze create a beautiful shimmer and can be combined with various colors for a modern twist. Pairing metallics with whites and deep greens can really elevate the festive atmosphere.” Plus metallics work well with New Year’s Eve trimmings, for those who like to let their Christmas decorations linger a bit.

You only need a few tasteful figurines to transform an ordinary tabletop into a holiday-themed vignette.

Sticking to one tone for trinkets artfully arranged on a console table or windowsill is a way to add holiday cheer that doesn’t look too busy. Add candles to your window display for an inviting glow that guests can spot as they come up your walkway. For the actual windows, Maggie Griffin of Maggie Griffin Design in Gainesville, Georgia, says nothing tops a traditional wreath. “I love a simple magnolia or boxwood wreath with a long silk ribbon with an understated bow. It’s classic and simple!” she says.

Repurposing leftover upholstery into stocking is a fun, easy DIY project.

If you’ve recently reupholstered, use leftover fabric scraps to create stockings that pair perfectly with your furniture. Or eyeball your existing chairs and couches and try to make a match. The room seen here—with walls painted Aubusson Blue by Annie Sloan—has striped stockings that make even the non-seasonal decor (the chairs) look more cohesive and intentional. Sloan takes the idea a step farther by matching her presents too. The chair, stockings, and gift wrap are all done in Sloan’s Ticking in Olive fabric.

No space for a 9-foot tree indoors? Try decking out a plant.

Designer Bailey Todd of White Cliff Studio in Columbus, Illinois, supports the desire to have multiple Christmas trees, or a decked-out tree and plant combo. “If you have lots of indoor tropical plants in your living room and don’t want to (or can’t) move them, decorate those too,” she says. “Just be sure not to use any heavy decor—keep garlands and ornaments light so you don’t damage any stems.” For a modern spin that’s also ideal for small spaces, skip the evergreen altogether and just go for the potted plant.

No need to completely change the palette of your space just to get it holiday-ready.

Greenfeld is a fan of a beautiful garland draped across the mantel. “When the garland gently hangs over the edges, it creates a soft, organic feel that perfectly frames the mantel and adds elegance without overwhelming the space,” he says. But doing so doesn’t mean you have to ditch your living room’s current, non-holiday color scheme. “I always suggest incorporating colors that complement the room so the garland enhances the space rather than compete with it.”

Subtlety not your thing? Go maximalist this Christmas with a themed tree.

“This year’s holiday decor is all about natural elegance and emotional warmth,” declares designer Anita Yokota, who decked the halls of the White House in 2023. “Real greenery, organic textures, and soft metallics create calm, layered spaces that feel alive.” Here, she’s adorned a tree in more muted, earthy tones alongside ornaments inspired by nature, like mushrooms. Golden accents complement all the browns and tans on the tree, adding just a touch of glamour.

DIY garland making can be a fun holiday activity at home for the whole family.

“I love when holiday decor feels gathered, not purchased,” says Jessica Whitley of Jessica Whitley Studio in Athens, Georgia. “Here, olive and rosemary branches bring sculptural softness to [the mantel’s] dark marble. A few metallic touches, like vintage bells or subtle shimmered ribbon catch the light and make the greenery feel festive without overpowering the space.”

A Christmas village—especially one that doubles as cozy mood lighting—is one way outside of your typical wreaths and trees to lend your home some holiday cheer.

Every surface serves as an opportunity to introduce some festive flair, as seen with this hallway table designed by Renae. Creating a Christmas village is a fun way for little ones to help with DIY Christmas decorations; they can paint buildings (available at craft shops or dollar stores like Dollar Tree) and even mold holiday-themed figurines, like a reindeer and or snowman, from clay. Keeping decor cozy and nostalgic aligns with this year’s trends, according to Renae. “For 2025, I’m all about the cozy, nostalgic vibe of Christmas,” she tells AD. “I love classic plaids, deep reds, and those warm, comforting touches that make any space feel like you’ve stepped into a Christmas movie.”

One simple method of giving your home a dash of holiday happiness? Add a simple runner in red-and-green plaid.

An easy way to weave holiday home decor into unexpected spaces is through rugs. Roll out a mat, runner, or larger carpet for a quick and cozy look. “Seasonal motifs, such as garlands, reindeer, or plaid, instantly make a space feel warm and festive for holiday gatherings,” says Maria O’Brien of Ruggable. Or opt for a yuletide spin on plaid, like a timeless tartan, as seen above. “Heritage-inspired patterns are having a moment, with classic red and green tones adding a touch of tradition to the home,” says O’Brien.

Bells and bows are tried-and-true Christmas classics.

Though model and actor Kara Del Toro lives in Los Angeles, she wanted her home to have a European feel for the holidays. “With our German roots, my mom and grandmother always brought little European touches into our holiday traditions,” she says. “So this year, I wanted to bring that nostalgia and old-world charm into my own home with a quaint European Christmas that complemented its Mediterranean architecture rather than competing with it.” To do so, she sourced cedar, pine, noble fir, olive branches, asparagus fern, red astilbe, and other seasonal flora to make her own garlands. She then added bells and red bows, embellishments you could picture at a Christmas market in Germany.

Pinecones, pomegranates, and oranges add some life to this festive tablescape.

To carrying that old-world feel over to her dining table, Del Toro decided to festoon it with fruit. “I layered all of the greenery with pears, pomegranates, dried orange slices, and pinecones, then added loads of candles for a little sparkle,” she says. “I love how something as simple as fruit or a beautiful branch can feel so festive when you put it all together.”

Exploring alternative options to your traditional Christmas tree? Think outside the box: Most greenery looks merry wrapped in lights and red bows.

If you already have a tree or large plant in your living room, make it the main attraction, like Del Toro did here. “One of my favorite decisions was skipping a traditional Christmas tree altogether,” she says. “I have an 18-foot olive tree named Olivia in my living room, and she’s already the focal point of the space. I thought, why compete with her? Instead, I climbed up on my ladder and dressed her with antique-style bells, twinkling lights, and hand-tied bows. It feels so fitting for a Mediterranean home, and I love that it’s a little unexpected.”

Embroidered napkins can add a festive flair to any holiday party.

If you’re hosting a holiday soirée, an embroidered cocktail napkin—like these, part of a 12 Days of Christmas set from Lettermade—is a small touch that makes a big impact, since your guests will be sitting with and handling them all night. Tying bows around the stems of your glassware is an equally charming detail.

Even if you go big for holiday decor, you don’t have to go against the grain. Tap into your existing color palette and style for Christmas decor if you’re craving a cohesive look.

“When decorating for the holidays, I like to build on the warmth and character of a home by incorporating rich, natural colors like olive, moss and burgundy that complement the existing interiors,” says Jennifer Sissom of Ryan Street Architects in Austin. Here, the team at Ryan Street did just that by mixing in hues that match year-round artwork in jewelry designer Kendra Scott’s Austin home.

Glassy ornaments make for a sleek winter wonderland.

In Scott’s home, the tree is decked with retro-looking mercury glass ornaments. “Looking ahead to holiday trends for 2026, I’m seeing a continued appreciation for vintage and collected pieces, particularly antique ornaments and aged mercury glass, which bring a softness and sense of history to holiday decorating,” says Sissom. “Overall, there’s a shift toward more personal, layered spaces that feel timeless rather than overly seasonal.”

What are 2026’s top trends in Christmas decor?

“This year, the holiday decor trends are grounded in a beautiful balance between nostalgia, whimsy, and sophistication,” says designer Taniya Nayak, a Marshalls and TJ Maxx home style expert. “We're seeing a continued appreciation for timeless holiday pieces, but with more personality, rich textures, and unexpected color combinations. It’s less about following a specific aesthetic and more about creating a home that feels festive, warm, and collected over time.”

While minimalism has had its moment in recent years, Nayak says the trend is shifting toward a more playful, maximalist approach to holiday decorating. “People are embracing more whimsical details like gingham, bells with luxe velvet bows, graphic black-and-white stripes, festive glassware, plaid throw pillows, or an unexpected accent like a faux pearl Christmas tree topper that adds personality and dimension without making the space feel overly styled,” she says. Rich jewel tones—popular last year—are still on trend this holiday season. Deep burgundies, emerald greens, and touches of gold or silver create a glamorous palette.

“I'm also loving food-inspired holiday decor,” says Nayak. “It's fun, fresh, and especially chic when styled in an elevated way.” This might mean glass-frosted ornaments that take the form of plump strawberries or an ice cream sundae. Sardine tins and shrimp have been especially popular when given the glass ornament treatment. Nayak also recommends decorating with citrus, such as tucking dried orange slices into greenery. “You can even bring this trend to your holiday table decor with pears, pomegranates, candles, and beautiful serving pieces,” she says. See Del Toro’s Christmas tablescape above for an example of festive fruit accents.

“My number one rule is that there are no rules when it comes to holiday decorating,” says Nayak. “The holidays are such a special time of joy, happiness, and family, so there’s no shame if you love a head start!” Everyone who has already had their Christmas tree up for a month can breathe a collective sigh of relief. That being said, Nayak also recommends easing into the season and decorating in stages. “You can start introducing cozy textures, scented candles, greenery, and warm lighting in early November. I also personally like to layer in chic serveware and velvet accessories that transition beautifully from Thanksgiving to Christmas. Then, as Thanksgiving approaches or passes, you can bring out more traditional holiday decorations,” she says.

If you're a procrastinator, that’s also perfectly fine.”There’s no deadline for creating a little holiday magic, and you don’t need to splurge or spend weeks decorating to make your home feel magical,” says Nayak.

Whether you’re looking to add small, unique holiday accents, like a beautiful decorative game set, a premium wool blend throw, or a silver-rimmed serving plate that inspires an entire holiday tablescape—or you’re looking to completely overhaul your space into a winter wonderland, it’s nice to have a game plan before you hit the shops.

Sometimes, a few thoughtful additions are all you need to make your home feel festive. As an added bonus, late decorators can also scoop up deals as holiday decor begins to be marked down.

How do I incorporate holiday decorations in more unexpected places throughout the house?

For those truly obsessed with the Christmas holiday, decorations don’t have to be confined to the living room. As shown above, designers have decked out kitchens, bedrooms, and hallways for the season; Button is even bringing the holiday spirit to her bathrooms. “Each year, I choose a new space to gussy up with festive decor,” she says. This year will be the bathrooms as a fun spot. I hide plastic animals with ribbons or mini wreaths on them for my children. It becomes a fun game to discover where the creatures have hidden themselves—sometimes peeking out from the tops of mirrors, or near the towel bar, or by the tub!”

What are some budget-friendly Christmas decor ideas that look expensive?

“Holiday decor doesn’t have to break the bank,” says Nayak. Small touches like festive kitchen accessories, tablescape accents, and natural elements such as garlands and wreaths are affordable ways to channel the holiday spirit. By prioritizing timeless, quality decor, you’ll create a well-curated atmosphere that will last for many seasons to come.

The centerpiece of holiday home decor is usually the tree, so placement is key. Samantha Stathis Lynch, designer and home style expert with Marshalls and TJ Maxx, says, “Christmas trees are often the focal point of holiday decor for those celebrating Christmas, so it’s important to have the tree in a room that is accessible and spacious. The living room or family room is often the most utilized; however, any room in your home can accentuate the tree—it’s all about preference.” Placing your tree in front of a window makes for elegant Christmas decor for your home’s exterior as well. (Is there anything more homey than seeing glowing Christmas lights in a window?) Or place your tree in the living room’s entryway so it can be enjoyed from adjoining rooms and add to your dining room’s ambiance or Christmas kitchen decor.

A cozy Christmas living room is all about texture, Thomas says. “Whether that’s velvet drapes, bouclé throw pillow covers, or a high-pile rug, textiles are the perfect way to add diverse textures to a room without making it feel overwhelming.”

Adding to that, Lynch recommends including subtle lighting, candles, and additional seating around your Christmas tree. “Ottomans or poufs can make any space the perfect area to gather around your tree and celebrate the season,” she says. Temporary seating near a Christmas fireplace is another option. Add throw blankets and trays with hot cocoa mugs to mimic ski chalet vibes. It’ll transform your living room into a cozy spot within a winter wonderland.

How to decorate living room windows for Christmas

Windows are even more real estate for your Christmas theme. “Symmetry across window panes is a largely popular seasonal trend that can be easily achieved with wreaths, candles, or garland,” Lynch says. “Place matching Christmas wreaths within the center of your home’s front-facing windows or candle holders and taper candles within each windowsill for a picturesque holiday home.”

Thomas, on the other hand, prefers more modern Christmas decor, like acrylic nutcrackers or matte white decorative presents. “Gathering these design-forward yet minimal trinkets in groups of three or five to form triangles—or what designers call three-point thinking—provides depth and intrigue to the eye,” he explains. “Windows are essentially built-in frames in a room. Knowing that, any window decor should lead with composition and proportion first, which is why less will always be more when it comes to windows.”

Thomas recommends using Command Clear Hooks for garlands that serve as mantel decor, emphasizing that “these should be in the arsenal of any DIY’er, as they are a great option for temporary solutions.” You could also use a tension rod in a pinch. “I’ve seen some rather creative implementations of this technique where folks will place a tension rod in between a passageway and use that to hang a garland. I will definitely be trying this method this year,” he adds. Before wrapping your garland around the rod, you can even spray-paint it green so it blends in better.

“When it comes to hanging stockings, I’m a traditionalist and I recommend investing in stocking hangers,” Thomas says. “These can be used year after year, and with so many options on the market, one can absolutely find an option that suits the rest of the decor. However, not everyone has real estate like a fireplace mantel to hang stockings, so I recommend some damage-free adhesive hooks.”

#4844. Bluefin to shut down perps, refocus on spot trading and tokenized RWAs

Bluefin will close its perps platform on Dec. 4, exiting a shrinking Sui market where it once handled over $500 million in daily trades.

Bluefin will discontinue its perpetual futures trading services on Dec. 4 to redirect resources toward spot trading and tokenized real-world assets.

“As the Sui team internalizes more of the network’s perps initiatives, we believe Bluefin’s resources are best focused on opportunities that complement that direction,” the decentralized exchange announced in a Thursday X post.

The platform urged users to close open positions by Dec. 4 and said withdrawals will remain available for an undetermined period after trading ends.

Bluefin said it accounted for 95% of Sui’s all-time perpetual trading volume and had more than 2.5 million accounts.

Bluefin handled as much as $575 million in perpetual futures trades on Feb. 14, 2024. The single-day volume dropped to $516,253 on Friday, according to DefiLlama data.

Bluefin is exiting a Sui perpetual futures market already experiencing a downturn. The network’s monthly perps volume has fallen from a peak of $4.85 billion in December 2024 to $312 million so far in November, according to DefiLlama.

#4843. Nvidia's Blackwell Chips Turn Up in China as Trump Floats Government Stake

Nvidia's Blackwell Chips Turn Up in China as Trump Floats Government Stake

Nvidia's most powerful chips have turned up at a Chinese data center tied to Alice Huang, the woman at the center of the scandal surrounding the company, as U.S. President Donald Trump said he could still take a government stake in the chipmaker.

Two Chinese firms installed Nvidia Blackwell hardware at the Yangtze River Delta Project, a data center in Shanghai, according to documents submitted to Chinese regulators and reviewed by Bloomberg. Blackwell chips have always required a U.S. license to ship to China.

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short NVDA with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

One of the firms, Shanghai Shuoyao, offered a GB300 NVL72 rack, which contains 72 Blackwell Ultra chips, as collateral for a 96 million yuan ($14 million) loan from Shanghai Innovation Bank, Bloomberg reported. Another, Shanghai Kezhan, described a GB200 server at the site when it took out a 90 million yuan loan from a leasing firm owned by a Shanghai government agency in late 2025. Kezhan's majority owner is a Tokyo firm that Chinese outlet Caixin has said is controlled by Alice Huang.

Using the rack's serial number, Bloomberg found it was built by Taiwan's Gigabyte, which declined to say whom it originally sold the hardware to. It's unclear how the rack reached China. Shanghai Shuoyao has said it is one of Megaspeed's service providers, describing the relationship as "limited to ordinary commercial cooperation." Megaspeed, the Singapore-based company Alice Huang founded, has denied wrongdoing, and Bloomberg said it had no evidence that Megaspeed diverted hardware to the site. Nvidia did not respond to Bloomberg's questions.

Alice Huang, whom U.S. intelligence suspects of working with Chinese intelligence during an affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, is at the center of a scandal that briefly cost him his job. The Commerce Department added Megaspeed to its trade blacklist this week.

Trump, who has said he "convinced" Nvidia's board to reinstate Huang, told the New York Post he was open to the U.S. government taking an equity stake in Nvidia, pointing to Intel, which handed Washington 10% of the company last year.

"I thought about it. I said, 'You know, maybe I should do it,' but I didn't bring it up at this point. It's probably not too late," Trump said.

He also said a pardon for Huang was "always an option" but that he didn't think it would be necessary, and urged Huang not to invoke his Fifth Amendment rights when he appears before Congress next week. Huang is due to sit for a closed-door interview with three House committees on December 1, and to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on December 3.

Speaking to reporters at his Mar-a-Lago estate on Friday, Trump again said Huang was not a security threat. Asked by AFP how he could be sure when the Justice Department would not confirm it had conducted a thorough investigation, Trump said his view was based on "information I have, which is a lot of information," The Straits Times reported. "I think he's absolutely fine," he said.

Polling analyst Nate Silver said on his podcast that Trump "absolutely" could be removed from office if he profited from selling advanced chips to China, and that a roughly 25% chance of impeachment and removal priced by prediction markets was "entirely reasonable."

On Polymarket, traders put a 20% chance on Trump being impeached and removed before 2028, and a 74% chance on him being impeached before his term ends. Kalshi priced a 21% chance of Trump being impeached and removed before his term ends in January 2029.

Nvidia shares were trading at $148.74 on Friday, down 0.4% on the day, according to Yahoo! Finance. That leaves them almost 10% below Monday's close of $165.05, when the stock jumped more than 30% on Huang's return.

#4841. Bitcoin supply metric hits 11-year low as new ‘capitulation’ signal arrives

The seven-day moving average of Bitcoin’s supply profit/loss ratio hit an 11-year low as BTC price losses month-to-date remain near 20%.

Bitcoin (BTC) is in a “meaningful stress phase” as an onchain profit-to-loss metric hits its lowest levels in 11 years.

Data from onchain analytics platform CryptoQuant reveals that Bitcoin on Thursday recorded its largest unrealized loss skew in more than 11 years.

The seven-day moving average of Bitcoin’s supply in profit/loss ratio has fallen to 0.825, below its parity level of 1. Values below 1 reflect a market state in which loss-making supply outweighs supply in profit.

The metric’s 30-day moving average remains higher at 1.27, reflecting the influence of recent price action on supply profitability. BTC/USD recorded its largest month-to-date loss of 28.8% as it dipped to $55,081 on Nov. 21.

“Historically, comparable conditions have appeared near major market bottoms, including the 2022 bear market,” CryptoQuant contributor CryptoZeno wrote Friday.

Bitcoin supply in profit/loss. Source: CryptoQuant

Bitcoin’s sell-side risk ratio, which divides total onchain realized profit and loss by the realized cap, has dropped to levels that typically accompany bear-market bottoms. Its 30-day moving average currently measures 16.52, reflecting a period of “capitulation” among investors.

#4838. Austria-supervised crypto firms report 20.4B euros in H1 trading volume

About 74% of accounts were based in other EEA countries, highlighting the market’s cross-border nature and putting Europe’s supervisory framework in focus, FMA said.

Crypto-asset service providers (CASPs) supervised by the Austrian Financial Market Authority (FMA) reported 20.4 billion euros ($22.37 billion) in trading volume for the first half of 2026.

About 74% of user accounts on these platforms were based in other European Economic Area (EEA) countries, particularly Germany and France, the Austrian financial supervisor said in a press release on Friday.

The 20.4 billion euros in the first half of 2026 exceeded the 17 billion euros reported for the full year of 2025, according to the FMA’s annual report.

The FMA said increasing cross-border activity creates a sharp focus on Europe’s crypto supervisory framework and highlights ongoing discussions about giving the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) an enhanced supervisory role over the industry.

In December 2025, the European Commission proposed transfering “direct supervisory competences” for key pieces of market infrastructure, including CASPs, to ESMA. If adopted by EU lawmakers, ESMA’s role in overseeing EU capital markets would resemble the framework of the US Securities and Exchange Commission.

In September 2025, France became the third European country to call for ESMA to take over supervision of major crypto firms, joining Austrian and Italian securities regulators.

#4837. Hackers Hit US Air Force Cloud System Running Air-Defense and Munitions Data

Hackers Hit US Air Force Cloud System Running Air-Defense and Munitions Data

Hackers have breached Cloud One, the U.S. Air Force’s flagship cloud computing platform, potentially jeopardizing a vast trove of sensitive tactical, personnel and logistics data, according to a Reuters report Friday that cited three people familiar with the matter.

The intrusion was discovered within the past month during work to upgrade the system, the report said, and investigators have called in U.S. Cyber Command, the military’s cyber force, to assess the damage.

“A breach here is a big deal,” one source told Reuters. It remains unclear who was behind the attack, how deeply they penetrated the system, or whether any data was stolen; the Air Force declined to comment on the specifics.

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Anthropic, Nvidia, Microsoft and more with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

Launched in 2017, Cloud One was built as a one-stop shop for the Air Force’s IT needs, pooling resources from Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle and Alphabet to run scores of applications.

Among the systems it supports are the Air Force’s Cloud-Based Command and Control, which collates air-defense radar and other data feeds across North America, and the Theater Integrated Combat Munitions System, which tracks bombs and missiles at more than 200 Air Force locations worldwide.

One source said intruders reached the platform’s control plane by exploiting a software flaw, though it’s not confirmed whether they took further action from there.

The breach has triggered real disruption. Officials paused ongoing migrations of back-office software to the platform, revoked administrator rights for some users, and blocked updates to existing applications, leaving personnel unable to apply fixes just as a fresh batch of serious software vulnerabilities was disclosed across the tech industry.

The incident lands amid a jittery stretch of cyberattacks and outages hitting U.S. federal institutions. Earlier this week, the CIA, the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence disclosed a breach of some unclassified systems, an intrusion investigators have tied to a suspected AI-powered hacking tool known as Artex.

That case fed growing alarm that artificial intelligence is accelerating the scale and sophistication of state-level intrusions, a concern now hanging over the Cloud One breach as well, even as its origin remains unknown.

For now, the Air Force says it continues to take “prudent measures” to protect its systems and mission capabilities, while the full scope of what was accessed, and by whom, remains under investigation.

That's a full year to decide whether you love it, and plenty of time to sort out the guest room before next Thanksgiving. If you'd rather lie down before you buy, Saatva viewing rooms in cities across the country—should you be lucky enough to live by one—have nearly every model on display, and no appointment is needed. If not, our editor’s have tested a number of their mattresses, and we can vouch for their feel and quality.

Saatva makes more than a dozen luxury mattresses, including the Saatva Rx mattress for chronic back pain and a memory foam hybrid mattress that layers cooling foam over coils. The four below made our list of the best Black Friday deals, and they vary by what’s inside.

Saatva's original mattress is an innerspring mattress with more than 1,000 recycled steel coils arranged in a dual-coil system, finished with a three-inch Euro pillow top for cushioning, so it feels closest to a traditional mattress: bouncy, supportive, and padded on top. Its three firmness levels cover most sleepers: Plush Soft for side sleepers and lighter bodies, Luxury Firm for every position and for couples who sleep differently (Saatva says this is the most popular), and Firm for stomach sleepers and anyone who'd rather lie on top of a mattress than inside it. It comes in 11.5- and 14.5-inch heights; go with the shorter one if an adjustable base is in your future, since the taller version isn't compatible.

Think of this as the Classic with natural latex in place of foam on top. Five zones of organic latex sit over individually wrapped recycled steel coils, under a cover of organic cotton and New Zealand wool, and the latex is GOLS certified organic with a GREENGUARD Gold rating on top of that (shorthand for good carbon footprint!). There's one feel: medium-firm (a 6 out of 10, per Saatva), with a buoyant push-back that's different from the slow sink of memory foam. AD's global editorial director and US editor in chief Amy Astley sleeps on one. "[My husband and I] both sleep warm and appreciate the vented airflow channels, which allow for circulation," she says in her review. She also found her lower back pain went away after the switch. "That alone is mattress gold!" she adds.

In most shared beds, somebody is compromising on firmness. The Solaire adjustable firmness mattress spares you both by putting a separate air chamber under each side, controlled by a wireless remote with 50 firmness settings (on queen sizes and up) and two memory buttons for saving your favorites. The comfort layers on top flip, too: latex side up for more bounce, foam side up for more give. Saatva recommends the softer settings for side sleepers and the firmer end for stomach sleepers. Pair a split king with Saatva's split adjustable base and each side can change its position as well as its firmness.

Saatva's first all-foam mattress skips springs entirely, so it molds to your body and lets you sink in slightly. It pairs two layers of cooling gel-infused memory foam with a high-density foam base that keeps movement from traveling across the bed. Contributor Bailey Berg, who considers anything north of 70 degrees hot, chose it for that gel foam and went with the firm option over relaxed firm to sleep cooler still. The dense base was the bigger surprise. "Both my partner and I are light sleepers: If one of us rolls over, the other one generally wakes up too," she says in her review. "After the first couple nights, I realized I hadn't been woken up by his movements (or by our dogs jumping on and off the bed) at all." Four years in, she reports no sag in the center, no dips where they sleep, and an organic cotton cover that has softened without pilling. If running warm is your main complaint, Saatva's newer all-foam model, the Contour5, adds a heat-dispersing CoolVent cooling system and a phase-change lumbar layer.

A shredded latex core cushions the head, neck, and shoulders in any position, and contributor Sydney Gore found that it eased her back issues. "You won't have to buy new pillows for years afterwards," she says in her best pillows review. Buy two and save up to $60. Send the second one to the guest room.

Saatva's organic sateen set is 300-thread-count long-staple cotton, GOTS certified organic, woven one yarn over and three under, which is what gives sateen its silky hand and soft sheen. The fitted sheet's deep pockets fit mattresses up to 16 inches tall, so it works on the taller Classic, and the set comes in white only. If you'd rather sleep on something crisp, contributor Katarina Kovac swears by the brand's percale for how airy the weave feels.

If a new mattress isn't in the cards this year, a topper is the next best fix. This one is three inches of organic natural latex quilted in organic wool under an organic cotton cover, and Saatva describes the feel as plush with medium firmness. It fits any mattress, Saatva's or otherwise, and the brand pitches it for softening a new bed during the break-in period or buying an old one a few more years.

For anyone who loves memory foam but not how warm it can run, this three-inch topper infuses the foam with graphite, which Saatva says draws body heat away, and wraps it in a breathable organic cotton blend cover. It's medium-firm with the contouring hug memory foam is known for, and Saatva recommends it for every sleep position, side sleepers especially. The foams are CertiPUR-US certified.

The softest of Saatva's toppers adds about two inches of down-alternative fill split into two chambers: a finer fiber on top for loft and a sturdier one underneath so you don't bottom out. Baffle-box stitching keeps the fill from drifting into one corner, a fitted skirt keeps the topper from sliding, and the 300-thread-count sateen cover is breathable. It's hypoallergenic and OEKO-TEX certified, which makes it an easy upgrade for a guest bed when you don't know who'll be sleeping in it.

The main draw is a one-touch zero-gravity button, which raises your feet to heart level and lifts your head and knees slightly for balanced support. There's also a head, full-body, and foot massage with three intensity levels, an anti-snore preset that tilts the head up seven degrees, under-bed LED lighting, and USB ports for your phone. Buy it with a mattress for $100 off. It works with every Saatva mattress except the 14.5-inch Classic and the youth and crib models, and adjustable bases can't be returned, so measure before you order.

With rounded edges and fluted drawers in natural oak, the Arden would look as at home in a beach house as in a city bedroom. Buy two and Saatva takes $200 off, which is how most people buy nightstands anyway.

This low-profile platform frame stands on slim legs that lift it off the floor, with a kiln-dried hardwood frame and plywood slats that let you skip the box spring. The back of the headboard is fully upholstered (it's shown in graphite velvet), so the bed can sit in the middle of a room without an unfinished side facing the door. It also works with Saatva's adjustable bases, and buying it with a mattress takes $100 off.

#4834. Brazil’s stock exchange pushes stablecoin launch back to 2027

Brazil’s stock exchange is working with six major financial institutions on a real-backed stablecoin that could launch as early as the first quarter of 2027.

Brazil’s stock exchange B3 is moving ahead with 2027 plans for a stablecoin pegged to the Brazilian real, after initially targeting a launch this year.

B3 is collaborating with six of Brazil’s largest financial institutions, Bradesco, BTG Pactual, Itaú Unibanco, Safra, Santander and XP, to launch the stablecoin in the first quarter of 2027, according to a Friday report by local news outlet Valor Econômico.

Called Open BRL, the stablecoin is to be issued by Banco B3, the exchange’s banking subsidiary, with each token backed by one Brazilian real. B3 will operate the underlying technology.

The initiative marks a new stage in the exchange’s digital asset strategy as Brazil’s financial industry prepares to bring traditional securities onto blockchain networks.

B3 first disclosed plans to introduce its own stablecoin in December 2025, targeting a launch in 2026.

As recently as July, the exchange was reportedly still preparing to launch a stablecoin called B3RL in the coming months, with infrastructure testing and integration with financial institutions scheduled for August and September.

B3RL was designed to be backed by Brazilian reais and secured by government bonds, and to facilitate blockchain-based trading of stocks and fixed-income securities starting in 2027.

It remains unclear whether Open BRL will replace B3RL or operate alongside it. Cointelegraph reached out to B3 for clarification but had not received a response by publication.

B3 also plans to introduce trading of tokenized shares in early 2027, initially using the same order book as conventional equities.

The platform would initially retain its two-business-day settlement cycle rather than introduce instant settlement, Humberto Costa, a B3 executive overseeing digital asset products, reportedly said in October.

Related: Brazil’s Halloween eve crypto deadline brings more tricks than treats

Costa also said B3RL would not handle settlement of tokenized shares at launch and that round-the-clock trading would require changes to Brazil’s regulatory framework.

Brazil’s Securities and Exchange Commission has been exploring a new regulatory framework for tokenization, presenting the progress of its dedicated working group at an industry meeting in October.

#4832. $7 Billion in Bitcoin Options Just Expired: Here’s What It Means

$7 Billion in Bitcoin Options Just Expired: Here’s What It Means

Nearly $6.8 billion worth of Bitcoin options expired Friday on crypto derivatives exchange Deribit, removing roughly a quarter of outstanding Bitcoin options positions from the exchange, according to CryptoQuant.

The expiration comes at a particularly difficult time for Bitcoin. The cryptocurrency traded near $61,000 ahead of settlement before dropping below $59,000 later Friday, extending a brutal November for crypto investors.

Friday’s expiry was considerably smaller than October’s $10.8 billion settlement, but the way traders positioned themselves tells a different story about market sentiment.

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Bitcoin with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

Options are financial contracts that give investors the right to buy or sell an asset at a predetermined price, known as the strike price. Call options generally benefit from rising prices, whereas put options can serve as insurance against a decline.

Nearly half of the outstanding $40,000 put positions were scheduled to expire on December 25. That doesn't necessarily mean traders expect Bitcoin to fall that far, but it shows that investors are willing to position themselves against such a scenario.

The estimated “max pain” price for Friday’s expiration stood at $70,000. That's the price at which option holders collectively receive the smallest payout at expiration, around 15% above Bitcoin’s price heading into settlement.

Bitcoin settled at approximately $61,600, leaving many put options with intrinsic value and higher-priced calls worthless.

The expiration does not mean $6.8 billion in Bitcoin changed hands. That figure is just the notional value of the underlying contracts, rather than the amount paid out at expiration.

What could affect Bitcoin's price is the unwinding of positions that market makers accumulated to offset their exposure to those contracts. As those hedges become unnecessary, buying or selling activity associated with them can disappear or reverse, potentially amplifying price movements in either direction.

Bitcoin still faces considerable selling pressure outside the derivatives market.

U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs registered their seventh consecutive trading session of net withdrawals on Wednesday, bringing November’s total to $5.39 billion.

Accelerating inflation, concerns over U.S. interest rates, and a renewed AI stock selloff have also put pressure on Bitcoin this week.

Traders were paying more for near-term volatility than for volatility further into 2027 ahead of the expiry, which likely means that concerns about Bitcoin’s near-term performance extend well beyond Friday’s settlement.

The next major options expiry is scheduled for Christmas Day, with contracts covering roughly 165,000 BTC, or about $10 billion at Friday’s settlement price.

#4830. Here’s what happened in crypto today

Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.

Today in crypto, the EU securities watchdog said it plans to overhaul its MiCA crypto register in 2027, bug bounty platforms are increasingly turning to artificial intelligence to manage a surge in AI-assisted security reports and Spain moved to grant its financial intelligence unit the power to freeze crypto accounts without prior judicial authorization.

The European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) is preparing an overhaul of its public crypto register nearly two years after its launch.

The European Union’s securities watchdog plans to replace its manual interim register under the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) with a searchable web-based platform around mid-2027, an ESMA spokesperson told Cointelegraph.

The new system will also maintain a version history for individual white papers to provide archives of changes.

MiCA’s transitional period ended in July, which meant that unauthorized crypto service providers had to wind down their EU operations or face multimillion-euro fines or other enforcement action. ESMA’s interim register serves as a public reference point for checking whether a crypto company is authorized in the bloc.

Crypto bug bounty platforms have expanded their use of artificial intelligence to keep up with a growing mountain of AI-assisted security reports.

Crypto-focused HackenProof said in October that it was using AI to triage 70% of submissions fully autonomously, aiming to hit 85% by the end of 2026. It said it received an average of about 6,100 bug reports a month in the third quarter, 2.4 times the reports from December last year.

Rival Immunefi last week said submissions to its platform rose 136% year-over-year in the first nine months of 2026, as it introduced a tool that can flag duplicates before a researcher submits a report.

Bug bounty programs pay independent researchers to find and report potential security flaws. AI has helped researchers uncover more genuine vulnerabilities, but has also swelled the volume of invalid and duplicate submissions, making it harder for security teams to identify the threats that need urgent attention.

It’s like “bringing a sword to a gunfight,” Dmitry Tokarev, founder of crypto wallet provider Bron, told Cointelegraph, referring to security teams that haven’t already adopted AI to sift through reports.

A decree published on Nov. 25 would give Spain’s financial intelligence unit, Sepblac, the power to freeze crypto accounts and halt transactions without prior judicial authorization when it suspects money laundering or terrorist financing.

The measures are scheduled to take effect on Jan. 25, 2027. Under Spain’s Constitution, the Congress of Deputies must vote to ratify or repeal the decree within 30 days of its promulgation. If ratified, crypto companies operating in Spain would have to comply with suspension orders or face financial penalties.

According to the decree, Sepblac would be able to suspend the use of a digital asset account or a business relationship for up to five business days, while transactions in progress could be held for up to 10 business days. Although the initial suspension of an account or transaction would be at the discretion of Sepblac, it could be extended by a court at the request of public prosecutors.

Nikolai Timofejev, head of licensing and regulatory affairs at legal consulting firm Prifinance, told Cointelegraph that crypto firms should start preparing for the change before it takes effect. “My advice is to treat it like an operational workstream with a named person who receives Sepblac’s orders,” he said. “Non-compliance amounts to a very serious infringement attracting fines starting at €150,000.”

#4829. Samsung Frame Pro TV Review, Tested by AD (2026)

A staple in most modern homes, televisions often war against the ongoing aesthetics of a space in their off-time. Masquerading as artwork, the Samsung Frame TV offers an alternative in the world of home entertainment that amplifies interior design instead of taking away from it.

Eagle eyes will have spotted the Frame across many of our home tours—including some celebrity abodes, like the living room of Jesse Tyler Ferguson’s New York pied-a-terre. With their art-forward ideology, it’s clear to see why the Frame line is favored by designers. After all, a big black screen is not really enhancing the visual impact of a living room.

As a design devotee and AD’s resident television and film-obsessive, I tried out the Frame Pro to see if it really measured up. Boasting the same matte finish display as the original model but with brighter picture quality, fully wireless outputs, and a bevy of technical upgrades, the Frame Pro has features to offer for tech purists and design-heads alike.

How much does it cost? Are there payment plans available?

The Frame Pro starts at $2,200—though is already marked down for Black Friday, and may drop further in price closer to the shopping holiday. Payment plans are available through Affirm, with options up to four installments, the lowest being $400 every two weeks.

The Frame Pro comes in three sizes, starting at 65 inches and going up in ten inch intervals to 85 inches. I opted for the smallest size to best fit my available wall space, and chose a white bezel border (brown and teak are the other colorways) to coordinate with the frames on the wall art in my living room.

A service coordinated the delivery window with me over email and helped to set up the television once they arrived to make sure it was functioning properly. Despite what the name would have you believe, the Frame Pro does, in fact, have attachable legs. The delivery service did not include mounting, so the team merely helped lift the Frame Pro onto my TV stand and set it up in a freestanding format.

What was the installation process like? How long did it take, and how many people?

The Frame Pro has a very slim mounting system consisting of two brackets. The installation kit comes with a paper template with the layout of the brackets printed on it. The process was fairly straightforward, though I wish the step-by-step manual had more text included rather than just showing images of the process.

Although the brackets have several slots to accommodate differing stud widths, we ran into an issue where the distance between the studs in our building didn’t quite align with the bracket slots to center it on the wall while also keeping the TV secure in the studs. In the end, we ended up hanging the TV ever so slightly off-center in order to keep the screws aligned with the studs. For peace of mind, we added drywall anchors and screws to the center-most slots of the bracket for some additional support to help distribute the weight a bit more.

Hanging the TV from the bracket was simple, and because the screw-in panels on the back are magnetized, it made it feel more secure when we slotted it into place. At just under 50 pounds, the TV wasn’t all that heavy, though because of the larger size, we did need two people (and another to guide the way) to lift it in place. The bezel is also magnetized, so the four pieces simply snap onto the exterior of the TV once you have it hung up.

Overall, the mounting process took us about two hours to complete but I think it could likely be decreased down to one hour (and possibly even less) had it not been for our particular issues with the stud distances that needed a lot of remeasuring and even a last-minute trip to the hardware store for a stud finder.

As the Frame’s main draw, I was most eager to see art mode in action. The artwork is selected either through Samsung’s Art Store (which requires a $4.99 per month subscription) or through personally uploaded photos to the SmartThings companion app. To really be convincing as artwork, the photos need to be high quality—you wouldn’t notice any blurriness when seeing the Mona Lisa at the Louvre, would you? For older artworks, I was able to find plenty of high resolution files available for free through museum or crowdsourced websites. Once you make sure its resolution matches the 4K sizing of the Frame (3,840 x 2,160 pixels), you simply upload the image and select if you want a matboard added to the border. If you upload a smaller size image, you can expect to see some amount of graininess once it loads on the screen. I chose a selection of paintings by Vincent Van Gogh, Georgia O’Keefe, and Claude Monet, among other artists with the rotating gallery feature. While essentially all the artwork I tested out looked beautiful on the screen, the paintings with thicker brushstrokes made me want to reach out and touch it to see if it was real.

I found that the art mode is most convincing when you’re in a well-lit room. Even though the TV brightness does adjust automatically—and has motion sensors so it only turns on when someone enters a room if you want to leave it on all day—the fact that it’s a screen becomes more obvious in low-light environments. Even at its lowest brightness setting, when in art mode in a dark room, the screen slightly illuminates the space, no longer tricking your eyes that it’s artwork.

In terms of the viewing experience, the Frame Pro certainly leveled up my weekly binge watches. The image is incredibly crisp, and when rewatching shows I’d seen before (I’m a creature of habit, what can I say), I noticed the colors were markedly more vivid than on my previous TV. The Neo QLED panel, a.k.a. mini LEDs, makes a big difference in the contrast of colors on the TV, and it’s all the more enjoyable to see ingenious set designs from my favorite shows and movies.

One of the big differences between the Frame Pro and previous models is the Wireless One Connect box. Where the regular Frame model has a slim transparent cord connected to the box that contains HDMI and other outputs, the Frame Pro is fully wireless, meaning the only cable coming out of the TV is the power cord. I have fairly speedy and reliable internet so there haven’t been any issues with connection being wireless. Plus, I love the clean look the lack of cords provides. The only time I noticed lag was when I tried using Chromecast from my phone to try and stream content. It took longer to load and had some clarity issues in the picture. That’s not true for everything I cast, as a movie I mirrored through AirPlay loaded easily, so I think it might have been due to an incompatibility with Google’s casting software or the phone it was being routed through.

I’ve had the Frame Pro for over a year now and haven’t noticed any difference in visual quality or functionality when watching different shows or movies. Style-wise, I’ve loved decorating around the Frame as the seasons change. The minimalist white base doesn’t detract from surrounding decor, like pumpkins during Halloween and garland and ornaments around Christmas. I’ve subbed in a few different pieces of artwork in the art library, particularly during hosting season when I want to curate a cozier vibe with an autumnal artwork or yule log video. The automatic software updates keep the TV functioning at a high level, even as streaming apps regularly change.

It’s safe to say that I’m keeping this TV for as long as possible. Even as someone who loves to watch shows and movies, I don’t want the entire design of my living room to revolve around a television. The slim design of the Frame really shifts the focus to the other furniture and decor in the space, and makes my space feel more centered around the memories made inside it.

#4826. 4 Scary Bitcoin Charts That Suggest This Bear Market Is Different

4 Scary Bitcoin Charts That Suggest This Bear Market Is Different

Bitcoin fell below $60,000 again on Friday as roughly $6.8 billion worth of Bitcoin options expired on derivatives exchange Deribit earlier in the day.

The largest cryptocurrency by market cap was trading at around $59,576 as of writing, down 1.58% on the daily chart after reaching an intraday high of $62,210.

As you might be able to guess based on the recent price action, Bitcoin's technical setup remains bearish—and there’s four charts in particular that tell the story.

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Bitcoin with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

The coin is trading well below its 50-day and 200-day exponential moving averages, or EMAs, which currently sit at $71,112 and $74,444, respectively, with the shorter-term average below the longer-term one—a classically bearish death cross pattern.

Its Relative Strength Index, or RSI, which measures the strength of recent price movements on a scale of 0 to 100, sits at 25.69, putting Bitcoin in oversold territory. Bitcoin is also approaching its 61.8% Fibonacci retracement level at $57,618, a potential support derived from the cryptocurrency's rally between its 2022 bottom and 2025 peak.

A sustained break below that level would put the recent lows back in focus. The next major Fibonacci retracement on the chart sits near $39,000, which would be an absolute nightmare for the markets. Thankfully for Bitcoin holders, BTC has bounced every time it touched it.

Perhaps more concerning for long-term Bitcoin investors, however, is what's happening to some of the most popular models used to make sense of Bitcoin's historical price cycles.

The Bitcoin Power Law model, popularized by physicist Giovanni Santostasi, attempts to explain Bitcoin's price growth as a mathematical function of its age.

Plotting Bitcoin's price and the time elapsed since its creation on logarithmic scales produces a relatively straight trend line. Two parallel lines establish theoretical upper and lower boundaries based on historical price extremes.

The appeal of the model was that Bitcoin's increasingly expensive bear market bottoms appeared remarkably predictable, despite the cryptocurrency's notorious volatility.

Bitcoin is now trading below what crypto analytics provider Bitbo sets as the theoretical support line of approximately $68,600, while the model's central regression puts its price near $193,400.

That's roughly 69% below its theoretical valuation, and 13% below what was supposed to be its historical floor.

The breach challenges one of the model's most attractive assumptions: that Bitcoin's minimum price increases predictably over time.

Bitcoin's four-year market cycle revolves around the halving, a programmed event that cuts the issuance of new Bitcoin tokens by 50% approximately every four years.

The most recent halving, in April 2024, reduced the reward miners receive for producing a block from 6.25 BTC to 3.125 BTC.

Bitbo's post-halving comparison chart takes the price performance following the 2012, 2016 and 2020 halvings and adjusts those returns to Bitcoin's price at the start of the 2024 cycle.

Had Bitcoin replicated its performance following the 2020 halving, it would currently be trading somewhere around $140,000. Matching the returns of its earlier cycles would imply prices of several hundred thousand dollars or more.

Instead, roughly 950 days after its most recent halving, Bitcoin is trading below where it was when that cycle began.

Diminishing returns are nothing new for Bitcoin as the asset grows larger. But the scale of the current underperformance raises questions about how useful previous halving cycles remain as a guide to future returns.

It also shows traders are a bit less enthusiastic about the upcoming halving vs previous times—maybe because Bitcoin is now more mainstream and the user base is more diverse and less interested in those technicalities.

The Bitcoin Rainbow Chart, which originated in 2014, uses logarithmic price curves and colored bands to classify Bitcoin's historical valuation.

The upper red bands represent speculative bubbles, while the lower blue and violet bands indicate historically depressed prices.

Bitcoin's price has dropped beneath even the violet region, humorously labeled “Bitcoin Dead,” in the supplied chart.

This isn't the first time the Rainbow Chart has struggled to accommodate Bitcoin's price movements. Its creator revised the model in November 2022 after the previous version failed to contain that year's market collapse.

The chart is ultimately a visualization of historical price behavior rather than a scientifically validated valuation model. Its latest divergence is another reminder of that limitation.

Bitbo's price prediction comparison brings together four different approaches to estimating Bitcoin's long-term value.

The Stock-to-Flow model, introduced by pseudonymous analyst PlanB in 2019, measures scarcity by comparing Bitcoin's existing supply with its annual issuance. Stock-to-Income expands on that concept by incorporating miners' transaction fee revenue and regularly updating its calculations.

The Power Law measures price growth over time, while the Halving Price Regression fits a curve using historical prices at halving dates, excluding much of the speculative activity between them.

In the chart's late-2026 projections, Stock-to-Flow puts Bitcoin near $397,535, followed by the Power Law at $198,495, Stock-to-Income at $173,412, and Halving Price Regression at $141,132.

Bitcoin is trading approximately 85% below the most optimistic of those projections and 58% below even the most conservative one.

None of these models directly measures how much money investors are willing to put into Bitcoin today, and arguably Bitcoin is now a different asset than the BTC we used to follow two years ago.

It’s possible that after the wave of ETFs, funds, derivatives, 401Ks, regulations, indicators tracking its price, and widespread access to retail investors, it’s these price-prediction models that need to change.

#4823. What was Coinbase worth while Nasdaq was closed?

A Thanksgiving buyer paid 106.24 USDC per Coinbase share. Whether that looked like a holiday rally depended on when you’d last checked the stock.

Tokenized stocks give investors another place to trade after the closing bell. Coinbase’s Thanksgiving tape shows why it still matters where else the shares changed hands and how many you want to trade.

On Thanksgiving afternoon, a buyer spent 125.49 USDC (USDC) on tokenized Coinbase shares while Nasdaq was closed. If you’d last checked the stock at Wednesday’s closing bell, that small purchase seemed to carry news of a holiday rally.

Coinbase had closed at $103.72, and the buyer on OKXICE paid 106.24 USDC per token, an apparent gain of 2.4%. But if you’d stayed for Wednesday’s after-hours session, you’d have seen the shares reach $106.91, according to brokerage Public.

From there, the very same token trade looked about 0.6% lower, valuing USDC at a dollar. However, the choice of where to start measuring was enough to turn a gain into a decline.

Related: Nasdaq exec pushes for common EU rules on tokenized securities

An investor in Germany had an even fresher price to go on. Early on Thanksgiving, 142 Coinbase shares changed hands on Tradegate at 97.50 euros apiece, roughly $107 at that day’s exchange rate.

What changed for the afternoon buyer was that they could open a wallet and buy Coinbase exposure over the holiday, and anyone following the stock could see exactly what that order cost.

Finding oneself on the other side of that trade with $10,000 worth of Coinbase to sell, the blockchain could tell you to four decimal places what someone had paid for just over one token, but could you get that price for 94?

#4821. Could AI Break Bitcoin? Not Yet, Research Firm K33 Says

Could AI Break Bitcoin? Not Yet, Research Firm K33 Says

Recent AI-assisted advances in mathematics have reignited worries about the cryptography underpinning Bitcoin, but there’s no evidence the network’s security has actually been broken, according to a report from research and brokerage firm K33.

The analysts, writing Friday, said AI’s rapid progress in math warrants closer attention to Bitcoin’s defenses, while cautioning against mistaking theoretical breakthroughs for a practical attack.

“Naturally, this has reignited fears surrounding the mathematical assumptions underpinning Bitcoin and modern cryptography,” they wrote, adding that the developments do not themselves offer a way to crack those systems.

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Bitcoin with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

The spark was a draft proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, one of math’s most famous open problems, published last week by Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge with help from the company’s Claude model.

As Decrypt reported, the proof passed independent computational verification, though academic review is ongoing. Its arrival stoked speculation about whether AI could eventually unravel the math securing digital assets.

K33 pushed back on the alarm. Bitcoin’s transaction signatures rely on elliptic curve cryptography, which hinges on how hard it is to derive a private key from a public one, even though the reverse is easy.

The firm noted that the Riemann proof provides no method for attacking that, and that the deeper “P versus NP” question at the heart of such fears remains unsolved. Even if someone proved P equals NP, K33 said, that wouldn’t necessarily yield a usable algorithm, or one that could run fast enough to recover a private key in any practical timeframe.

Conversely, proving P does not equal NP wouldn’t guarantee Bitcoin’s safety either, since faster attack algorithms could still emerge.

The report lands as the broader industry takes the AI-cryptography threat increasingly seriously. The Ethereum Foundation recently flagged AI as a more urgent danger than quantum computing, given its ability to find software flaws and sharpen existing algorithms.

K33 noted the Ethereum Foundation has doubled its protocol security team and recommended the Keccak-256 hash function for a post-quantum transition it aims to complete by 2029.

The takeaway, per K33, is vigilance without panic.

AI’s mathematical leaps deserve monitoring, and crypto networks are right to harden their cryptography against future threats, but as things stand, Bitcoin’s defenses remain as sound as they were at launch, with no demonstrated compromise.

#4816. China sets March 2027 rollout for blockchain identity regulations

China published new regulations on blockchain-based digital identities on Nov. 27, establishing a framework for identity verification and interoperability across government institutions and private-sector platforms.

The regulations, which will take effect on March 1, 2027, were jointly issued by 11 government departments, including the People’s Bank of China and the Cyberspace Administration of China.

Under the rules, China’s national blockchain network will provide the infrastructure for a digital identity system operated by entities authorized by the country’s cyberspace regulator, in cooperation with identity authentication and credential providers.

Digital identities powered by blockchain technology can allow users to verify their identity or credentials across platforms without disclosing unnecessary personal information.

According to Chinese state-backed media outlet China Net, the identity chain will bring together multiple institutions “to achieve multi-party consensus through blockchain technology.”

The regulations are part of China’s broader push to expand blockchain adoption, with the country targeting 2030 to largely complete its national blockchain infrastructure while maintaining restrictions on cryptocurrency-related activities in mainland China.

Individuals and organizations will be able to voluntarily register digital identities and use verifiable credentials to disclose specific information, such as educational or professional qualifications, without necessarily revealing all the associated data.

Platforms and digital identity service providers will be required to follow data minimization requirements, collecting only the information necessary for identity verification. They will be prohibited from using that data for cross-platform profiling or targeted advertising.

The regulations aim to address barriers to identity verification across regions, industries and platforms. They also encourage interoperability with digital yuan and the adoption of distributed digital identities in sectors including finance, taxation, transportation and customs.

Related: China targets 2030 for its national blockchain network buildout

#4814. Why fertile male killifish outlive their peers

Why do some individuals of the same species live significantly longer than others? In evolutionary biology and aging research, this question is often linked to a trade-off between reproduction and survival. The underlying idea is that energy and resources invested in reproduction may lead to compromises in repair and maintenance, thereby hindering a long life. Thus, the assumption is that particularly successful reproduction at a young age comes at the cost of a shorter lifespan.

#4811. Bitcoin whales pile into BTC despite shrinking profit cushion

CryptoQuant data shows Bitcoin whales are breaking with historical fourth-quarter selling patterns despite a market downturn.

Bitcoin whales are bucking the years-long trend of trimming their balances toward the end of the year. Instead, they are accumulating the cryptocurrency despite falling prices and dwindling unrealized profits.

According to onchain analytics firm CryptoQuant, whales added about 121,000 Bitcoin (BTC) to their holdings between Sept. 30 and Nov. 21, taking their combined balance to nearly 2.95 million BTC, despite a price decline of nearly 30% over the same period.

CryptoQuant defines whales as addresses holding between 1,000 and 10,000 BTC. Unrealized profits across addresses holding at least 1,000 BTC have shrunk 81% to $23.8 billion from $124.7 billion on Sept. 30.

The report, supported by crypto lending platform CoinRabbit, notes that whales have historically reduced their holdings toward the end of the year in both bull and bear markets. Since 2017, whale balances have declined in seven of the nine previous fourth quarters, with 2019 and 2020 being the only exceptions.

Meanwhile, dolphins, a term referring to addresses holding between 100 and 1,000 BTC, have slightly reduced their holdings. The group shed about 15,169 BTC, representing 0.28% of its holdings.

Related: Bitcoin supply metric hits 11-year low as new ‘capitulation’ signal arrives

The accumulation comes as Bitcoin has lost about 32% of its value since the beginning of the year, with the cryptocurrency trading at around $59,750 at 6:45 p.m. UTC on Friday, according to TradingView data. The report notes that borrowing against Bitcoin holdings may be allowing some large investors to access liquidity without selling their assets.

According to CryptoQuant, among CoinRabbit users with more than $100,000 in loans, the number of Bitcoin-backed loans increased by 298.9% month-on-month in October, while total loan volume fell by 16.2%.

The pattern contrasts with October 2025, when the number of Bitcoin-backed loans fell by 3.7% but total loan volume increased by 122.8%.

CryptoQuant suggested that the shift toward more frequent but smaller loans could indicate that large holders are borrowing to raise cash instead of selling Bitcoin.

Crypto tax firm Summ suggested the shift could also be linked to the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF). Since January, participating jurisdictions have begun requiring crypto exchanges and other service providers to collect users’ transaction data for tax authorities, with the first international exchanges of tax-related information expected in 2027.

Summ CEO Shane Brunette said holding BTC and borrowing against it are rational responses “to a world where every sale is visible.”
